speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help narrow this down, did these symptoms start suddenly or have they been developing over a few days?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scarlet Fever (or potentially Kawasaki Disease given the age and rash description, but the rhinorrhea points more toward a viral exanthem like measles or roseola with secondary rash; however, the specific description of a facial rash sparing the perioral area appearing after fever and upper respiratory symptoms is highly suggestive of Measles or a specific viral exanthem). Let me clarify: The timeline of fever followed by a rash, specifically with a "facial rash sparing the perioral area," is a classic presentation for certain viral exanthems or scarlet fever. Given the age (11) and the specific sequence (fever/rhinorrhea/headache -> rash), could you tell me if the rash has a "sandpaper" texture or if you see any red lines on the sides of your tongue (strawberry tongue)? Also, have you been around anyone else with similar symptoms recently?
